subject: Scandit ESG Supplier Assessment
text:
Dear Vendor,

At Scandit, we are committed to responsible procurement and to working with suppliers who share our values on environmental, social, and governance (ESG) matters. As part of this commitment, we have recently launched our Sustainable Procurement Policy and are conducting lightweight ESG assessments of our strategic suppliers.

As a valued partner, we would like to include your company in this process. We want to keep this as simple as possible for you, and have set out two ways you can provide the information:

Option 1 - Complete our short ESG Questionnaire (preferred)

We have prepared a short questionnaire that should take no more than 15 minutes to complete. You can access it here: ESG Questionnaire.

Option 2 - Share existing documentation or public information

If you prefer not to complete the questionnaire, we can work with information you already have available - such as a sustainability report, ESG policy, or website page. To allow us to complete the assessment on our end, it would be helpful if the information you share covers the following topics:

Environment

• 

Whether you have an environmental or sustainability policy, and where to find it

• 

Whether you track environmental data such as energy consumption, travel emissions, or waste

• 

Any environmental improvement actions or initiatives you have in place

Social

• 

Whether you have a policy on labour standards or employee wellbeing

• 

How you ensure fair and safe working conditions for your employees

• 

Any diversity, equity, and inclusion (DEI) policies or initiatives

• 

How you address risks related to discrimination, harassment, or human rights

Governance

• 

Whether you have a Code of Conduct or ethics policy, and where to find it

• 

Any internal controls for managing compliance, risk, or financial integrity

General

• 

Any ESG improvements or initiatives implemented in the last 12–24 months

• 

Your openness to collaborating with Scandit on ESG topics going forw

subject: Re: Fw: End-to-end MRI pipeline @ Cerebriu (Callum from Encord)
text:
Hi Callum,

I appreciate you digging out the information from our last meeting, such that I don't have to re-explain.

Consensus merge: While we did had developed a usable solution ourselves, we have opted for a change in our workflows such that merging of landmarks is no longer a prioritized feature.

SPACE sequence: The Siemens SPACE image type I seem to remember was used as a proxy for your internal "MRI Phycics" knowledge. In other words it was not so much about the technical solution that would allow ourselves to configure a filter, but more whether you would be able to also do such a configuration.

We do currently not have resources available to take such a call. Should you wish to have a look on how images are labelled in the MRI field I encourage you to have a look at e.g. the BIDS standard, and tools like dcm2bids. This tool allows you to provide a configuration file to do filtering (albeit based on nifti sidecars, but these values are pulled from Dicom metadata - both private and public tags).

Kind regards,

text:
Hi Joe,

Lovely choice of menu!

We’re really looking forward to welcoming you and your guests. We’ll need
the final starter and main selections for everyone 7 working days in
advance, by 23rd June, but it would be great to get these confirmed sooner
rather than later if possible.

The space incurs a minimum spend of £2,000 for exclusive use for the
duration of the evening. This is inclusive of VAT but excludes service
charge. All food and drink go towards your minimum spend, and there is no
additional hire fee. To secure the booking, we require a deposit of £1,000 (50%
of the minimum spend) which will be deducted from your final bill on the
day. Please let me know when is it a good time to send over a paylink.

Our sommelier has also put together some wine recommendations to pair with
both the fish and sirloin options. Drinks will be charged based on
consumption, and if you’d like us to keep an eye on the spend and let you
know during the event, just let me know and I’ll make sure the wider
management team is aware.

Wine recommendations:

   - *Albariño, Bodegas Chaves 2024 £66; Bordeaux, Les Allées de Cantemerle
   2015 £74*
   - *‘Destination’ Chardonnay, Journey’s end, Stellenbosch 2024 £89, Town
   Pauillac 2020 £90*
   - *Pouilly Fuisse 1er Cru Les Crays, Eric Forest 2023
   £130;‘Guidoalberto’ Super Tuscan, Tenuta **san Guido 2021 £135*

We’ll also need a seating plan ahead of the evening. If you’d like, we’d be
happy to provide name cards for dinner as well.

We’ll keep some space reserved for you upstairs. Are you happy for your
guests to order anything they’d like from the menu while they’re there?

Once again, we’re really looking forward to welcoming you. If you have any
questions or would like to make any tweaks, please don’t hesitate to call
or email me, I want to make sure everything is perfect for you.

Best,

subject: Re: Fw: End-to-end MRI pipeline @ Cerebriu (Callum from Encord)
text:
Hi Callum,

Its actually quite the opposite. In the current landscape we do not see any vendor being able to provide a solution that would cover our need for curation (here meaning both choosing which data to annotate and choosing what data to use for which application, i.e. trianing/validation splitting and such). The complexity of the MR data metadata subspace simply requires too much domain knowledge that a non-MR dedicated platform is unlikely to work. You would likely argue, that your platform can be made so flexible that we can do the configuration ourselves, but I see little value in that compared to doing a full solution ourselves. As an example see dcm2bids: It can almost do what we would need from a technical solution perspective, but the setup still requires significant domain knowledge to setup a configuration file. Even with dcm2bids being open-source we have opted for building an in-house solution, as the primary work is not in the technical solution  - its in the domain knowledge needed to make it work.

As such we are only looking for a stable annotation tool from a 3rd party provider and if Redbrick are going to focus on doing that (i.e. adapting "doing one thing but doing it great") that would only be a possitive in our book.

Kind regards,

[https://www.cerebriu.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/logo-Cerebriu-sign.png]

I don't see much gained from this interaction from our side, so I will instead point you to another open source project that is starting to do what you want to be doing: dcm2niix and their "guessBIDStype".
